about: Cases where KiCad's reference disagrees with the maker's datasheet, checked by hand against the datasheet text. A field listed here that fails against KiCad is scored as right (the report lists it as a reference erratum) when ours is what the datasheet says. A number under "ours" (e.g. the pitch) must match ours, or none of the case's errata apply: the other fields (pads, pin 1, courtyard) are excused only when we built the datasheet's package. "reference": {"footprint": <a footprint in the set's references>} scores the case against that footprint instead, when KiCad's own reference is another variant of the package, or against the maker's own recommended land (a reference named "Maker:...", its numbers copied by hand from the datasheet's land drawing; it gives no courtyard, so none is scored). "reference": {"renumber": {"<KiCad pad>": "<datasheet pin>"}} scores the case against KiCad's footprint with those pads renumbered, when the datasheet numbers the same package's pads otherwise.

symbol_names.why: Diodes AH1806 datasheet (AH1806.pdf) p1 pinout and p2 pin table: SC59 (the -W package, p5) pin 1 VDD, pin 2 GND, pin 3 OUTPUT. KiCad's Sensor_Magnetic:AH1806-W has 2 OUTPUT, 3 GND.

reference.why: Diodes AH1806 datasheet (DS36104 Rev. 8-2) p1 Pin Assignments, SC59 top view: pin 2 (GND) alone on one side, pins 3 (OUTPUT) and 1 (VDD) on the other; p2 pin table 1 VDD, 2 GND, 3 OUTPUT. KiCad's SC-59 footprint numbers the lone pad 3 (SOT-23 order), so its pads 2 and 3 are scored as the datasheet's 3 and 2.

NXP PCA9557.pdf Rev. 7 p2 ordering table: PCA9557BS is HVQFN16 SOT629-1; p20 Fig 25 SOT629-1: body 4 x 4 x 0.85 mm, e 0.65, Dh/Eh 1.95-2.25, b 0.23-0.38; p26 Fig 29 footprint: pitch 0.65, pad 0.30 x 1.10, solder land 2.0 x 2.0. KiCad's reference HVQFN-16-1EP_3x3mm_P0.5mm_EP1.5x1.5mm is the 3 x 3 mm 0.5 mm package, another variant. Scored against KiCad's 4 x 4 mm 0.65 mm VQFN-16 with a 2.1 mm exposed pad instead (Texas RGV0016A, already in the set's references; Dh/Eh nom 2.1 like SOT629-1), so pad 1, pitch, pads and courtyard are all checked; it replaced an erratum that excused those fields whenever the pitch was 0.65.

symbol_names.why: Microchip/Atmel doc0014.pdf (AT27C256R) p2 pin table 'O0 - O7 Outputs' and the 28-lead PDIP diagram; the datasheet has no D0 or Q0. KiCad's Memory_EPROM:27C256 names them D0-D7.

courtyard.why: doc0014.pdf p11 28P6 PDIP: D 36.703-37.338 mm, E1 13.462-13.970 mm (our body); KiCad's DIP-28_W15.24mm courtyard is drawn around a generic, shorter DIP-28 body.

symbol_names.why: ST SM6T datasheet (the copy at farnell.com/datasheets/1761324.pdf) p1: 'Unidirectional and bidirectional types', the unidirectional symbol drawn K / A; p3 table of order codes 'SM6T100A/CA': the A suffix is the unidirectional part, CA the bidirectional one. KiCad's Diode:SM6T100A, itself described as unidirectional, names its pins A1 / A2, the bidirectional part's names.

reference.why: TI ucc3895.pdf p52 J (R-GDIP-T**) ceramic DIP 4040083/F: 20 pins, 2.54 mm pitch, rows 7.62 mm apart, no land pattern or hole size printed. KiCad's reference for the part is DIP-20_W7.62mm_LongPads, the hand-soldering variant (2.4 x 1.6 mm pads) of the same DIP-20; the datasheet gives no reason for long pads, so the plain DIP-20_W7.62mm is scored.

Wolfspeed C3D02065E datasheet (Rev. 7, Nov 2024) p6 Recommended Solder Pad Layout: tab 5.60 x 5.85, lead pads 2X 1.30 x 2.00 at 2X 2.27 from the centre line, 2X 2.50 from the tab; p5 TO 252-2L top view and pin table: pin 1 CATHODE (left lead), 2 ANODE (right lead), 3 CATHODE (tab). KiCad's TO-252-2_TabPin1 works its pads out from the package (3.5 x 2.0 leads, 7 x 7 tab) and numbers the tab 1; the maker's land is the truth (Oliver 2026-10-21). The datasheet draws no courtyard.

onsemi FDMT800100DC/D p8, CASE 507AR (98AON95711G, issue C) RECOMMENDED LAND PATTERN: pads 1-4 1.25 x 1.27 at 2.00 pitch, 1.50 gap to the 7.00 x 5.50 drain pad, drain tabs 8-5 1.25 wide reaching 1.15 above it (6.65), 9.42 overall; pin 8 above pin 1. Pad 9 is the drain pad. KiCad's PQFN_8x8 is drawn from the FDMT80080DC sheet and merges each net into one pad (3 pads: G 1.13 x 1.1, S 0.48 x 5.1, D 6.33 x 7.1), so ours can never match it pad by pad; the maker's land is the truth (Oliver 2026-10-21). The datasheet draws no courtyard.

symbol_pins.why: onsemi FDMT800100DC/D (Rev. 2, Nov 2022) p1 Electrical Connection: pin 1 G, pins 2-4 S, pins 5-8 D, and the bottom drain pad D (unnumbered on the sheet; numbered 9, after the leads, as every exposed pad here). KiCad's Transistor_FET:FDMT800100DC has 3 pins (1 G, 2 S, 3 D) for its merged-pad PQFN_8x8.

symbol_names.why: onsemi FDMT800100DC/D (Rev. 2, Nov 2022) p1 Electrical Connection: pin 1 G, pins 2-4 S, pins 5-8 D, and the bottom drain pad D (unnumbered on the sheet; numbered 9, after the leads, as every exposed pad here). KiCad's Transistor_FET:FDMT800100DC has 3 pins (1 G, 2 S, 3 D) for its merged-pad PQFN_8x8.

reference.why: ROHM p3 Figure 5 (above): the fin is GND and the middle lead is a cut N.C. with no land. KiCad's TO-252-2 numbers the fin pad 2, so its pad 2 is scored as our fin 4.

symbol_pins.why: ROHM BDxxFC0 series datasheet (TSZ02201-0G2G0A600040-1-2, Rev.007) p3 Figure 5, Pin Description (Without Enable) TO252-3: 1 Vcc, 2 N.C. (not connected inside the IC, leave open), 3 Vo, FIN GND. The fin has no number on the sheet; ours numbers it 4, after the leads. KiCad's Regulator_Linear:BD33FC0FP numbers the fin 2 (1 VCC, 2 GND, 3 VO), the TO-252-2 convention, and drops the cut N.C. lead. Same copper on the same nets either way.
